desc: Ideation: identify that the graph remains bipartite, characterize moves as internal missing-edge additions or component merges, and note that for odd N the total play length parity is fixed by M.
Implement brute-force canonical Sprague-Grundy computation for small graphs and collect P/N tables to reveal the eventual pattern.
Extend brute force to small N and infer the exact closed-form winner criterion for even N, including isolated vertices, active odd components, complete bipartite components, and missing-edge parity.
Verify the inferred rule against brute force for small N and prove the key cases.
Implement the linear-time solution using BFS/DFS or DSU to compute component bipartition sizes, internal edge counts, and the derived criterion.
Test the implementation on the provided samples and edge cases such as N=1, M=0, already terminal complete bipartite graphs, multiple isolated vertices, and graphs containing even cycles.
